references.text: The Pharisees said that Jesus cast out demons by the prince of demons—a parallel accusation against Jesus as in Luke 11:15.
Jesus mentions Beelzebul by name and says they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, which directly connects to the accusation that he casts out demons by Beelzebul.
Matthew's parallel account where the Pharisees accuse Jesus of casting out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of demons.
Mark's parallel account where the scribes say that Jesus has Beelzebul and casts out demons by the prince of demons.
Jesus' response to the accusation in verse 15, where he argues that Satan cannot cast out Satan and asks by whom their own sons cast out demons.
The crowd accuses Jesus of having a demon, reflecting the same type of accusation as in Luke 11:15.
The Jews accuse Jesus of having a demon, a similar charge to the accusation that he casts out demons by Beelzebul.
Beelzebul (Ekron's god Baal-Zebub) is mentioned in connection with King Ahaziah sending messengers to Baal-Zebub, the god of Ekron—the background for the name Beelzebul as the prince of demons.
